newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY MVM ANNOUNCES TENDER FOR NEW POWER PLANTS.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY MVM ANNOUNCES TENDER FOR NEW POWER PLANTS.

text.p: Hungary's electricity supplier MVM's will on Wednesday formally announced a tender for the contruction of 2000 megawatts of new Hungarian capacity, a company official said on Tuesday.

"The announcement will be fulfilled tomorrow (Wednesday)," Istvan Bakacs, MVM's strategic director told Reuters. "There will be two closed tenders for 1,000 MW each, the first for smaller units and the second for larger plants which have a longer lead-in time".
The tender for smaller capacity plants of 20 to 200 MW will be for commissioning between 2001 and 2003 while the second tender will be for larger units to go on line between 2003 and 2005.
Bakacs said the final result of the two tenders, which will run in parallel, will not be known for at least a year.

"It is a two-stage bidding with a short technical round now which they have to submit without any price or commercial conditions by the end of September, followed by technical negotiations which, depending on the number of bids, will be two to three months," he said.

The second stage, the final formal bidding, will last five months in order to give the bidders time to submit the detailed documentation required by the regulators for the preliminary licences, which include the environment licence, Bakacs said.
He added that this period may be extended at MVM's discretion by up to 60 days.
"It might happen that a large number of bids will require an extension and we will consider that sympathetically as we want a fair competition," Bakacs said.
"I expect the submission date to be some time next May and under the existing rules evaluation will take two months, meaning about one year from now for the final decision."

Bakacs said current investors in the Hungarian power generation industry were all considering bidding. Currently these include RWE , Tractebel , AES and Powergen , who have taken stakes in existing Hungarian power stations.
But Bakacs added other utilities who had not yet invested in Hungary were showing interest.

"RWE will definitely be bidding, and AES is most likely," he said. "But I feel a big interest from companies which did not participate in (Hungary's energy) privatisation until now who either were not successful or were not prepared to take risks with existing assets."
There will be no limit on how much of Hungary's 7,500 MW total capacity one constructor will be allowed to operate, he added.

A German consortium of RWE Energie AG and EVS operates 800MW of coal-fired capacity at Matra, north-east Hungary, Tractebel of Belgium has oil- and gas-fired capacity at Dunamenti, in central Hungary, while AES runs three oil- and coal-fired units at its Tisza site, in the east.
RWE Energie AG and EVS AG announced plans last month to build two new 500 MW power plants at Matra, while AES told Reuters earlier all three of its Hungarian units were likely to enter the tender.
